title: Universal Japanese property from finite normalization of finite type domains
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Suppose that for every homomorphism $R\to S$ of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] with $S$ an integral domain, $S$ is N-1 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. Then $R$ is universally Japanese [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring]: for every such finite type domain algebra $S$, the domain $S$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain].

proof.text: Fix a finite type domain algebra R → S and a finite extension L of K = FractionRing S. Mathlib FiniteDimensional.exists_is_basis_integral gives a finite K-basis e of L integral over S, without separability or Noetherian hypotheses. Let B = Algebra.adjoin S (Set.range e). Mathlib Algebra.finite_adjoin_of_finite_of_isIntegral makes B finite over S.

For z in L, use IsLocalization.exist_integer_multiples_of_finite to clear all coordinates e.repr z by a common nonzero d in S. The basis expansion gives d z = sum_i a_i e_i in B. Both d z and d lie in B, and d remains nonzero in L because S embeds into K and K embeds into L. Thus z = (d z)/d, and IsFractionRing.of_field proves that L is a fraction field of B.

Give L its composite R-algebra structure. Since B is finite over S, it is finite type over S; Algebra.FiniteType.trans makes it finite type over R. Being a subring of L, B is a domain. The hypothesis gives IsN1 B (FractionRing B). Transport this finite normalization to integralClosure B L using IsLocalization.algEquiv and AlgEquiv.mapIntegralClosure. Module.Finite.trans then makes integralClosure B L finite over S.

The finite S-algebra B is integral over S by Algebra.IsIntegral.of_finite. Hence isIntegral_trans maps integralClosure B L into integralClosure S L. This map is S-linear and surjective: IsIntegral.tower_top shows that an element integral over S is integral over B. Module.Finite.of_surjective makes integralClosure S L finite over S. Since L and S were arbitrary, R is universally Japanese.
